title: Configuration item metadata ordering is not consistent

timeline.message:
Fixing ordering for multiple classes that share same configuration property

Fixes gh-26217
timeline.author: Dmitry Pavlov
Dmitry Pavlov
Dmitry Pavlov

timeline.body:
If `o1` is of `GROUP` type and `o2` is of `PROPERTY` type, comparison is made except for `this::isDeprecated`, but `o1` is of `PROPERTY` type and `o2` is of `GROUP` type, it includes `this::isDeprecated` to compare. Isn't it inconsistent?

Wouldn't it be better to always compare `this::isDeprecated` regardless of type?

reply.body: This is not possible. Sort is applied after filtering of items to have just one type: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/400b98700db7e5075888cba7bc50277b0d9a085b/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-tools/spring-boot-configuration-processor/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/configurationprocessor/metadata/JsonConverter.java#L42-L43

timeline.body:
> This is not possible. Sort is applied after filtering of items to have just one type:

Sorry to keep bothering you. In the case of `GROUP` type, `this::is Deprecated` will always be false. Isn't it okay to use `itemComparator` regardless of type?

reply.body: I don't use it for items, only for groups - take a look at `compare(ItemMetadata o1, ItemMetadata 02)`, diff can be misleading

timeline.body: @zeldigas thank you for making your first contribution to Spring Boot. I've polished things in d610f3c . In particular, the `sourceType` is not mandatory and that was breaking with a NPE in that case.
